items.q: What is the circle in Greene's model of consciousness?
items.a: The familiar loop of thoughts and routines, **wide in childhood** and **shrinking into sameness** with age.
From Latin *sub limen*, **up to the threshold** of a door out of that circle.

items.q: Why does the sublime feel both good and bad?
items.a: It mixes the **pain of the unfamiliar** with the **pleasure of novelty**.
**Focus deeply** on an ordinary thing and tell yourself **you will remember this moment**.

items.q: How do phones change our sense of time?
items.a: They break thought into **tiny fragments**, losing the **slow rhythm** children have.

items.q: Where does awe come from, per Dacher Keltner?
items.a: **Shifting quickly between small and large spatial scales**, like a forest opening onto a vista.

items.q: Why does filming an experience dull it?
What lesson does the Dersu Uzala story carry?
items.a: **Sensory attention is intelligence**, and it atrophies in the **sameness of city life**.

items.q: What should you do with frustration when searching for your life's task?
items.a: Treat it as a **signal you're on the wrong path**, not just a bad feeling.
